name: How do you decide between log chinking and standard caulking for gap repair?

mainEntity.name: How do you decide between log chinking and standard caulking for gap repair?

acceptedAnswer.text: Chinking is a textured, flexible sealant designed for wide, uneven gaps between larger logs, while energy seal or caulking is smooth and formulated for narrow, milled joints. Chinking accommodates significant structural movement and resembles traditional mortar, making it ideal for hand-hewn logs. Smooth caulking works best in seams under an inch wide, such as around door jambs, window bucking, and corner corners. Choosing the right material ensures the seal does not tear as the cabin settles through seasonal temperature swings.
acceptedAnswer.description: Chinking is used for wide, irregular gaps between large logs, while caulking is best for narrow seams under an inch, such as around window and door trim.
